title: Enterprise Dedicated Onboarding: Heuristics for Priority, Cost/Latency Trade-offs, and SLA Tiering
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Context: We get frequent enterprise requests for reserved/dedicated capacity where customers ask for specific latency SLOs, guaranteed throughput, and GPU family commitments. Current intake is ad-hoc, and SEs create bespoke proposals that are inconsistent and slow. Goal: standardize the intake and triage so we can make fast, consistent decisions (accept, negotiate, or decline) and produce repeatable SLA templates and scaling policy recommendations.

Scope: build a lightweight intake form + scoring rubric, define three SLA tiers with example reserved throughput/GPU profiles, produce scaling policy templates (steady, burst, preemptible fallback), and hand off templates to Solutions Engineering and Sales for rapid proposal generation. This ticket covers product-level decisions and artifacts; implementation of UI/automation is tracked separately (ENG-20912).

Key intake fields to capture: expected sustained RPS or token/sec, peak burst multiplier and duration, 95/99th latency target (ms), model family & estimated context length, token composition (prompt vs generation), expected tokens per request, data residency/compliance needs, support window & SLA penalty sensitivity, committed spend and contract term, estimated QPS growth over 12 months, tolerance for model variant fallback, and preferred GPU families (if any).

Deliverables: intake form spec, prioritization scorecard spreadsheet, three SLA tier templates (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with example GPU families and pricing guidance, scaling policy templates (min/max, burst credits, preemption tolerance), and a short operations runbook for SE handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form spec documented and reviewed by SE and Sales
Scoring rubric implemented in shared spreadsheet with sample scoring for 3 historical inbound requests
SLA tier templates (Bronze/Silver/Gold) created with reserved throughput, suggested GPU class, and sample latency SLOs
Scaling policy templates available for low-latency steady workloads, bursty workloads, and cost-optimized preemptible configurations
PRD and one-pager for Sales/SE distribution reviewed and approved by PM lead
decision_log: 2026-02-11: Agreed scoring weight distribution: Revenue(30%), Latency sensitivity(25%), Compliance(20%), Engineering effort(15%), Strategic value(10%). Rationale: prioritize high-revenue / latency-sensitive customers while surfacing compliance needs.

2026-02-12: SLA tiers defined: Bronze = best-effort reserved with soft latency guidance (p95 < 400ms), Silver = reserved throughput with p95 target < 250ms and reasonable burst credits, Gold = reserved throughput + dedicated premium GPUs (A100/H100) with p95 < 150ms and SLA credits. Decision favors offering burst credits over infinite bursting to protect capacity.

2026-02-14: GPU family guidance: recommend H100/A100 for Gold, A100/T4 mix for Silver depending on model size, and L4 or T4 for Bronze/embeddings. Note: explicit H100 requests require capacity validation and price uplift.

2026-02-16: Autoscaling policy templates: (1) latency-first: small min nodes with aggressive scale-up, (2) throughput-first: larger min nodes to absorb spikes, (3) cost-optimized preemptible: use spot instances with graceful degradation to lower-quality model variant. Chosen default for Silver/Gold is latency-first with bounded burst credits.

2026-02-17: Pricing assumptions reviewed with Finance: base reserved throughput priced per vGPU-hour with tiered discounts and explicit burst credits billed separately. Final pricing model to be validated in pilot.
next_steps: Host 90-minute workshop with SE, Sales, Finance, and Ops to walk through rubric and SLA tier examples (target: 2026-02-22)
Update shared intake spreadsheet with scoring formulas and add three anonymized historical requests for calibration
Create PRD for intake UI and automation (linked to ENG-20912) and hand off to Eng PM
Draft customer-facing SLA one-pager and template contract language with Legal review
Pilot: run 2 incoming enterprise requests through the new workflow and collect feedback from SEs and affected customers
